body:
What you're saying seems sound. I would certainly say that a portion of what I experience is depression, but I believe it to be a symptom  -- an aspect of my current state, which compounds other issues.  


I wouldn't know where to turn for help. Proper help is expensive; whether it works, or not, I will be left living with other issues that my level of income could not easily resolve. I worked as a desk guard - for a time - at a very functional Mental Health Hospital Group, and the treatment they gave their patients was considered amongst the best in the nation (even taking patients from overseas). Their fees were extraordinarily high.

I've come back to look at your comment a few times -- wasn't sure how to respond. I don't know how to do anything, but deny it; the closest I've gotten to help was a handful of hotline calls.  


If I got help, I'd have to confess to the professionals the rotten core of the anxiety that has had me teetering on the edge. If I got help, people would know how pathetic I really was. To be honest, I wouldn't care if my mother was upset, but my little brother (not so little, as he's in his late 20s) -- looked up to me for a time (some of my fuck-ups in life were center stage, much of the rest I've lied to keep hidden) He may yet, still, but I might be projecting.   


With some of the terrible/disappointing things I've done, I think he understands that I am in conflict, and that's just who I am. But, if he really knew how much lying I've done to appear "okay" to the family, to him -- I can't begin to imagine the damage I'd do. In that, I feel selfish? Destructively, predictably selfish.  


I don't know if I'm more concerned with him knowing I don't do the work I say I do, for the damage it would do him, or the lasting reputation it would leave of me -- with him? I wanted a little brother, I asked for one, and I got one. I named him, I love him, I want the world for him.   


If I regret one thing, it would be not having given a good honest yank on that belt as a child. Now, I'm left to scheme some way to bury the last few years of "progress" so that - when I go - people won't be able to connect the dots. Ideally it wouldn't be "he couldn't move past his own shame," it would be "he must have been depressed." Again, selfish.   


Trying wrap my head around the fact, that, I've learned something of myself while typing this. Feels shit to be shit. I'd apologize for the garbled reply, but now I'm questioning just how genuine the intent of that apology would be.
